results.title: Rescission of Climate-Related Disclosure Rules
results.key_finding: This rule represents a complete rescission of climate disclosure requirements that directly benefits regulated financial industry entities by eliminating transparency obligations, exhibiting strong indicators of regulatory capture through ESG rollback and disclosure weakening.

results.title: Holding Foreign Insiders Accountable Act Disclosure; Correction
results.key_finding: This rule is a routine technical correction fixing a typo and removing references to a law Congress repealed in 2005, with no substantive policy changes that would indicate regulatory capture.

results.title: Registered Offering Reform
results.key_finding: This rule systematically dismantles multi-layered investor protections by expanding shelf offerings, weakening disclosure requirements, diluting WKSI standards, and preempting state securities laws - all framed as 'modernization' but collectively representing major deregulation favoring capital formation over investor protection.

results.title: Enhancement of Emerging Growth Company Accommodations and Simplification of Filer Status for Reporting Companies
results.key_finding: This rule uses 'simplification' rhetoric to systematically expand disclosure accommodations originally designed for small and emerging companies to a much broader class of issuers, representing a significant rollback of investor transparency requirements that primarily benefits mid-sized public companies, their underwriters, and private equity sponsors seeking easier public market exits.

results.title: Rescission of Policy Regarding Denials in Settlements of Enforcement Actions
results.key_finding: This rule eliminates a 54-year-old policy that prevented settling parties from publicly denying SEC allegations, representing a major win for financial institutions seeking to minimize reputational damage from enforcement actions while substantially weakening the deterrent effect of SEC settlements.

results.title: Semiannual Reporting
results.key_finding: This rule proposes halving mandatory disclosure frequency from quarterly to semiannual reporting, a significant reduction in investor transparency that primarily benefits corporate issuers at the expense of investors who rely on timely financial information.

results.title: Technical Amendments to Rule 610(e) of Regulation NMS and to Delegation of Authority To Grant or Deny Exemptions From Rule 610 of Regulation NMS
results.key_finding: This is a purely ministerial technical amendment correcting a cross-reference error created by prior renumbering, with no substantive policy changes, exemptions, or weakening of investor protections.

results.title: Form PF; Reporting Requirements for All Filers
results.key_finding: This rule proposes to roll back post-financial-crisis reporting requirements for private funds, reducing regulatory visibility into hedge funds and private equity at a time when private markets have grown substantially and pose increasing systemic risk.

results.title: Concept Release on Consolidated Audit Trail and Other Audit Trails and Data Sources
results.key_finding: This concept release signals potential receptivity to industry arguments for scaling back the Consolidated Audit Trail by framing cost, privacy, and complexity concerns prominently, though as a preliminary comment solicitation it does not yet constitute actual regulatory rollback.

results.title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
results.key_finding: This is a routine technical update to the EDGAR filing system with no meaningful signs of regulatory capture—it primarily addresses administrative filing procedures rather than substantive regulatory policy.

results.title: Performance-Based Investment Advisory Fees
results.key_finding: This is a routine, statutorily-mandated inflation adjustment to qualified client thresholds that actually strengthens investor protections by preventing threshold erosion, showing minimal signs of regulatory capture.

results.title: Application of the Federal Securities Laws to Certain Types of Crypto Assets and Certain Transactions Involving Crypto Assets
results.key_finding: The rule creates multiple categorical exemptions that could remove large swathes of crypto assets from securities regulation, with a novel 'separation' mechanism that allows assets to exit SEC jurisdiction—a framework that primarily benefits large crypto exchanges, issuers, and financial institutions seeking regulatory arbitrage.

results.title: Publication or Submission of Quotations Without Specified Information
results.key_finding: The proposal to narrow Rule 15c2-11 to only equity securities may exempt debt and other securities from broker-dealer due diligence requirements, potentially reducing investor protections in OTC markets, though the truncated excerpt limits full assessment.

results.title: Holding Foreign Insiders Accountable Act Disclosure
results.key_finding: This rule implements Congressional legislation that strengthens investor protections by extending insider disclosure requirements to foreign private issuers, representing an expansion rather than contraction of regulatory oversight.

results.title: Form N-PORT Reporting
results.key_finding: This rule reverses 2024 transparency enhancements by extending filing deadlines and reducing reporting frequency from monthly to quarterly publication, directly responding to 'market participant feedback' in ways that benefit fund companies at the expense of investor access to timely portfolio information.

results.title: Investment Company Names Form N-PORT Reporting; Extension of Compliance Date
results.key_finding: The SEC extended Form N-PORT compliance dates by approximately 4 years, delaying investor access to standardized data that would verify whether investment funds' names accurately reflect their holdings.

results.title: Delegation of Authority To Grant or Deny Exemptions From Rule 612 of Regulation NMS Under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934
results.key_finding: This rule is a routine technical amendment correcting an outdated cross-reference with no substantive policy implications and no indicators of regulatory capture.

results.title: "Small Business" and "Small Organization" Definitions for Investment Companies and Investment Advisers for Purposes of the Regulatory Flexibility Act
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be a routine technical adjustment for inflation rather than clear regulatory capture, though expanding 'small business' definitions inherently reduces the population of firms subject to full RFA impact analysis in future rulemakings.

results.title: List of Rules To Be Reviewed Pursuant to the Regulatory Flexibility Act
results.key_finding: This is a procedural rule mandated by statute that creates a systematic review pathway focused on burden reduction; while not itself evidence of capture, it establishes a framework that industry can exploit to advocate for rollbacks without equivalent emphasis on investor protection.

results.title: Delegation of Authority to the Director of the Division of Investment Management
results.key_finding: This is a routine administrative delegation that streamlines confidential treatment decisions for investment adviser filings; while it could marginally ease industry access to confidentiality protections, it does not substantively alter disclosure standards or represent clear regulatory capture.

results.title: Technical Amendments to Commission Rules and Forms
results.key_finding: This appears to be a routine technical housekeeping rule correcting outdated cross-references and obsolete provisions, with no substantive evidence of regulatory capture or industry-favoring rollbacks.

results.title: Technical Amendments to Commission Forms
results.key_finding: This is a purely administrative technical amendment correcting the SEC's physical address on forms from the old 450 Fifth Street NW location to the current 100 F Street NE headquarters, with no substantive regulatory changes that could indicate industry capture.

results.title: Extension of Compliance Date for Disclosure of Order Execution Information
results.key_finding: This compliance date extension represents a modest accommodation to industry operational concerns that delays but does not eliminate expanded order execution transparency requirements.

results.title: Concept Release on Residential Mortgage-Backed Securities Disclosures and Enhancements to Asset-Backed Securities Registration
results.key_finding: This concept release signals potential rollback of post-2008 RMBS disclosure requirements under the framing of 'capital formation' and 'issuer access,' revisiting protections enacted after the financial crisis that were specifically designed to address opacity in mortgage-backed securities markets.

results.title: Acceleration of Effectiveness of Registration Statements of Issuers With Certain Mandatory Arbitration Provisions
results.key_finding: The SEC is abandoning its historic role as gatekeeper against mandatory arbitration provisions, effectively blessing corporate charter terms that eliminate investors' ability to bring class action securities fraud suits in court—a fundamental shift that dramatically favors issuers and financial institutions over retail investors.

results.title: Commission's Rules of Practice
results.key_finding: This procedural rule change modestly favors issuers by eliminating automatic stays during appeals of offering effectiveness determinations, but represents a narrow administrative adjustment rather than substantive deregulation of disclosure or enforcement standards.

results.title: Form PF; Reporting Requirements for All Filers and Large Hedge Fund Advisers; Further Extension of Compliance Date
results.key_finding: Three successive compliance deadline extensions totaling over 2.5 years for hedge fund reporting requirements strongly suggests industry capture, as regulators repeatedly accommodate industry resistance to Dodd-Frank mandated transparency measures.

results.title: Extension of Compliance Dates for Electronic Submission of Certain Materials Under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934; Amendments Regarding the FOCUS Report
results.key_finding: This is a procedural compliance extension rather than substantive deregulation, representing modest industry accommodation that delays but does not eliminate electronic reporting modernization requirements.

results.title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
results.key_finding: This is a routine technical/administrative update to the EDGAR filing manual with no substantive policy changes, exemptions, or rollbacks—it simply updates filing system documentation and provides no evidence of regulatory capture.

results.title: Extension of Compliance Date for Required Daily Computation of Customer and Broker-Dealer Reserve Requirements Under the Broker-Dealer Customer Protection Rule
results.key_finding: This six-month compliance extension delays but does not eliminate an investor-protective rule requiring daily reserve computations, representing modest industry accommodation rather than significant regulatory capture.

results.title: Policy Statement Concerning Agency Referrals for Potential Criminal Enforcement
results.key_finding: This policy statement systematically weakens the SEC's criminal referral pipeline by creating new procedural barriers and adopting industry-favored 'overcriminalization' framing, directly benefiting financial institutions and executives who face reduced criminal prosecution risk for securities law violations.

results.title: Withdrawal of Proposed Regulatory Actions
results.key_finding: This rule represents an extraordinary wholesale withdrawal of 14 investor protection proposals across virtually all SEC-regulated domains, including explicit rollback of shareholder rights provisions, strongly indicating coordinated regulatory capture favoring financial industry interests over investor protection.

results.title: Form PF; Reporting Requirements for All Filers and Large Hedge Fund Advisers; Further Extension of Compliance Date
results.key_finding: This second compliance extension for enhanced hedge fund reporting requirements suggests industry pressure to delay transparency obligations, though the modest 4-month delay and preservation of underlying rules indicates limited rather than severe capture.

results.title: Concept Release on Foreign Private Issuer Eligibility
results.key_finding: This is a neutral concept release seeking comments on FPI eligibility criteria; insufficient text is provided to determine whether the eventual outcome would expand or restrict exemptions, though the framing around 'accommodations' warrants monitoring.

results.title: Regulation SBSR (Reporting and Dissemination of Security-Based Swap Information) and Security-Based Swap Data Repository Rules; Extension
results.key_finding: The SEC is extending compliance forbearance for certain security-based swap reporting requirements until 2029, continuing a pattern of delayed implementation that has stretched over a decade since initial adoption, though the core reporting framework remains operational.

results.title: Form N-PORT and Form N-CEN Reporting; Guidance on Open-End Fund Liquidity Risk Management Programs; Delay of Effective and Compliance Dates
results.key_finding: The SEC is delaying already-finalized transparency requirements for open-end fund portfolio reporting by two years, directly benefiting fund companies while reducing investor access to timely information about fund holdings and liquidity risks.

results.title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
results.key_finding: This is a routine technical/administrative update to the EDGAR filing manual incorporating system changes, with no substantive policy changes that would indicate regulatory capture.

results.title: Form PF; Reporting Requirements for All Filers and Large Hedge Fund Advisers
results.key_finding: This appears to be a minor technical corrections rule rather than a substantive policy change, with insufficient detail in the excerpt to identify meaningful regulatory capture signals.

results.title: Investment Company Names; Extension of Compliance Date
results.key_finding: This compliance extension delays but does not eliminate investor protections against misleading fund names, representing moderate industry accommodation rather than outright regulatory capture.

results.title: Delegation of Authority to Director of the Division of Enforcement
results.key_finding: This rule removes enforcement efficiency by centralizing subpoena authority that had been delegated since 2009, creating bureaucratic friction that will likely slow or reduce SEC investigations into securities law violations.

results.title: Extension of Compliance Dates for Standards for Covered Clearing Agencies for U.S. Treasury Securities and Application of the Broker-Dealer Customer Protection Rule With Respect to U.S. Treasury Securities
results.key_finding: The SEC granted the financial industry a one-year delay in implementing Treasury clearing requirements designed to reduce systemic risk, prioritizing industry operational convenience over timely investor and market protections.

results.title: Technical Amendments to Commission Rules and Forms
results.key_finding: This rule is a routine administrative housekeeping action with no substantive policy changes; it corrects typographical errors and updates cross-references without expanding exemptions, weakening enforcement, or reducing disclosure requirements.

results.title: Form PF; Reporting Requirements for All Filers and Large Hedge Fund Advisers; Extension of Compliance Date
results.key_finding: This rule grants hedge fund advisers a 3-month compliance delay for enhanced reporting requirements that were already given a 13-month implementation period, representing a modest accommodation to industry but not a substantive weakening of investor protections.

results.title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
results.key_finding: This is a routine technical/administrative update to the EDGAR filing system that implements previously adopted disclosure rules, showing no signs of regulatory capture and instead facilitating enhanced transparency through structured data formats and new short-selling disclosure requirements.

results.title: Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 122
results.key_finding: SAB 122 rescinds crypto-asset custody accounting requirements that major banks and crypto platforms heavily lobbied against, replacing mandatory liability recognition with discretionary general standards that reduce investor visibility into custodial risks.

results.title: Electronic Submission of Certain Materials Under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934; Amendments Regarding the FOCUS Report
results.key_finding: This is primarily a technical modernization rule that enhances regulatory transparency through mandatory electronic EDGAR filing and structured data requirements, with minimal signs of regulatory capture.

results.title: Daily Computation of Customer and Broker-Dealer Reserve Requirements Under the Broker-Dealer Customer Protection Rule
results.key_finding: This rule represents a genuine strengthening of customer protection through mandatory daily reserve computations for large broker-dealers, though the reduced debit item percentage (3% to 2%) offers a modest concession to industry that partially offsets the enhanced compliance burden.

results.title: EDGAR Filer Access and Account Management
results.key_finding: This is a technical infrastructure modernization rule focused on improving EDGAR security and account management, with no meaningful indicators of regulatory capture or weakening of investor protections.

results.title: Commission's Organization and Program Management Regulations
results.key_finding: This is a routine administrative housekeeping rule updating SEC regional office contact information with no substantive regulatory impact on the financial industry or investor protections.

results.title: List of Rules To Be Reviewed Pursuant to the Regulatory Flexibility Act
results.key_finding: This is a procedural notice required by statute (RFA) rather than a substantive deregulatory action, but the review framework it initiates is structurally tilted toward industry interests by focusing solely on compliance costs without mandating equivalent analysis of investor protection benefits.

results.title: Private Fund Advisers; Documentation of Registered Investment Adviser Compliance Reviews
results.key_finding: This document is a minor technical correction fixing a publication date placeholder and contains no substantive regulatory content to analyze for capture signals.

results.title: Private Fund Advisers; Documentation of Registered Investment Adviser Compliance Reviews
results.key_finding: The SEC is passively codifying a court-ordered rollback of private fund investor protections without pursuing appeals or alternative regulatory approaches, effectively accepting the elimination of oversight that hedge funds and private equity firms actively litigated against.

results.title: Conforming Amendments to Commission Rules and Forms
results.key_finding: This is a routine technical housekeeping rule making conforming amendments and error corrections with no substantive policy changes that would indicate regulatory capture.

results.title: Covered Clearing Agency Resilience and Recovery and Orderly Wind-Down Plans
results.key_finding: This rule appears to strengthen financial stability oversight rather than weaken it, implementing robust margin and wind-down requirements for systemically important clearing agencies consistent with post-crisis reform objectives.

results.title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
results.key_finding: This is a routine technical update to the EDGAR filing system that implements previously adopted disclosure requirements (including cybersecurity disclosures) and shows no signs of regulatory capture—it is purely administrative infrastructure maintenance.

results.title: Regulation NMS: Minimum Pricing Increments, Access Fees, and Transparency of Better Priced Orders
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be a genuine market structure reform that reduces tick sizes and access fees to benefit investors, though the tiered complexity and exchange fee model accommodations suggest some industry influence in implementation details.

results.title: Form N-PORT and Form N-CEN Reporting; Guidance on Open-End Fund Liquidity Risk Management Programs
results.key_finding: This rule strengthens rather than weakens investor protections by increasing portfolio reporting frequency and transparency, with no significant capture signals beyond moderately extended compliance timelines.

results.title: Qualifying Venture Capital Funds Inflation Adjustment
results.key_finding: This rule implements a congressionally mandated exemption expansion rather than reflecting direct SEC capture, though the underlying EGRRCPA statute itself may reflect industry influence in reducing oversight of smaller venture capital funds.

results.title: Financial Data Transparency Act Joint Data Standards
results.key_finding: The excerpt contains only procedural/administrative content (agency identifiers, docket numbers, comment instructions) without substantive rule provisions, making capture analysis impossible—the actual data standards that would reveal industry influence are not included in the provided text.

results.title: Regulatory Flexibility Agenda
results.key_finding: This is a procedural notice required by the Regulatory Flexibility Act publishing the SEC's rulemaking agenda—it contains no substantive rule changes and therefore shows no signs of regulatory capture.

results.title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
results.key_finding: This is a routine technical/administrative update to the EDGAR filing manual with no substantive policy changes that would indicate regulatory capture; it actually expands filing infrastructure for swap execution facility oversight.

results.title: Registration for Index-Linked Annuities and Registered Market Value Adjustment Annuities; Amendments To Form N-4 for Index-Linked Annuities, Registered Market Value Adjustment Annuities, and Variable Annuities; Other Technical Amendments
results.key_finding: This rule appears to genuinely expand investor protections by bringing index-linked and market value adjustment annuities under existing SEC registration and disclosure frameworks, implementing Congressional directives rather than exhibiting capture signals.

results.title: Regulation S-P: Privacy of Consumer Financial Information and Safeguarding Customer Information; Correction
results.key_finding: This is a purely ministerial correction to citation formatting in the Federal Register and contains no substantive policy changes that could indicate regulatory capture.

results.title: Special Purpose Acquisition Companies, Shell Companies, and Projections; Correction
results.key_finding: This is a purely technical correction to formatting language in the Federal Register and contains no substantive policy changes that could indicate regulatory capture.

results.title: Regulation S-P: Privacy of Consumer Financial Information and Safeguarding Customer Information
results.key_finding: This rule primarily strengthens consumer data protection by imposing new breach notification requirements, expanding safeguard obligations to more entities, and broadening covered information—showing minimal signs of regulatory capture and instead reflecting enhanced investor protection.

results.title: Customer Identification Programs for Registered Investment Advisers and Exempt Reporting Advisers
results.key_finding: This rule represents a genuine expansion of regulatory oversight rather than capture, extending anti-money laundering customer identification requirements to investment advisers who were previously exempt from Bank Secrecy Act obligations.
